contributions: Formalizes label propagation as a harmonic function minimizer with a closed-form solution via the graph Laplacian
Introduces label spreading with regularization parameter α to handle noisy labels
Describes belief propagation and loopy belief propagation for probabilistic inference on graphs
Connects collective classification as a precursor to GNN message-passing
Demonstrates 94% accuracy on Karate Club with only 2 seed nodes
Reviews benchmark results showing classical methods lag GNNs on citation networks but remain competitive in feature-free regimes
limitations: Pure label propagation cannot correct noisy labeled nodes since they are held as hard boundary constraints
Loopy belief propagation double-counts evidence on graphs with short cycles (especially triangles), producing overconfident marginals
Classical methods lack node attributes and perform substantially worse than GNNs on citation networks where feature signal is discriminative
Influence maximization is NP-hard and #P-hard to approximate exactly
The approach assumes homophily holds, which the chapter notes is not universal and breaks down in some settings
methods: The chapter covers iterative label propagation where unlabeled node estimates are updated by averaging neighbors' values until convergence, with a closed-form harmonic solution F_U* = (I - Ã_UU)^(-1) Ã_UL Y_L. Label spreading extends this with a regularization parameter α balancing graph smoothness against label fidelity via F* = (1-α)(I - αS̃)^(-1) Y. Belief propagation frames inference as message passing on a factor graph with prior, edge, and evidence potentials. The chapter also covers the Linear Threshold Model and Independent Cascade Model for influence maximization, both proven submodular with a (1-1/e) ≈ 63% greedy approximation guarantee.
results: On the Karate Club graph with 2 seed nodes, label propagation achieves ~94% accuracy on 32 unlabeled nodes. Benchmark comparisons on Planetoid splits (20 labeled nodes per class): Label Propagation scores 68.0% (Cora) and 45.3% (CiteSeer); Label Spreading scores 72.4% and 50.2%; GCN scores 81.5% and 70.3%; APPNP scores 83.3% and 71.8%; C&S post-processing scores 84.2% and 73.4%. Three nodes (2, 8, 28) are occasionally misclassified due to structural ambiguity at faction boundaries.
tldr: This chapter presents classical graph-based semi-supervised learning methods—label propagation, label spreading, belief propagation, and collective classification—along with influence maximization and epidemic diffusion models, showing how label and information propagation share a unified mathematical framework.
